summary: The note covers the Smart Neighborhood Initiative (SNI), a city plan unveiled on September 5th, 2023 at the Smart Cities Conference to bring smart technology to neighborhood services such as waste management, energy, transportation, public safety and environmental monitoring. It lays out a rollout timeline from October 2023 through mid-2024, built on a Smart Infrastructure Framework of sensors, cameras and Wi-Fi hubs. It also notes privacy and security concerns, integration challenges, and the role of resident feedback in finalizing the implementation plan.
one_line: The city unveils its Smart Neighborhood Initiative, a phased 2023-2024 rollout of smart waste, energy, traffic, safety and environmental technology.
key_facts: Mayor Patricia Johnson, City Council members and local technology experts unveiled the smart technology plan on September 5th, 2023, at the annual Smart Cities Conference.
The Smart Neighborhood Initiative (SNI) is spearheaded by Councilwoman Rebecca Gates and grew out of years of research, pilot programs and consultations.
The Smart Infrastructure Framework is an interconnected network of sensors, cameras and Wi-Fi hubs; deployment is expected to begin November 15th, 2023, at major intersections and public spaces.
Chief Technology Officer Michael Davidson said the infrastructure will serve as the "eyes and ears" of the neighborhood.

Smart bins with sensors will be deployed on October 20th, 2023, to track waste levels in real time and alert sanitation workers; Sanitation Commissioner Laura Phillips said they will also help plan recycling programs.
Smart lighting with LED lights that adjust to natural light and the presence of people will be installed starting December 1st, 2023.
Smart grid pilot projects are set for the second quarter of 2024 and would let residents sell excess solar or wind energy back to the grid.

Smart traffic lights are planned by January 2024, with priority signals for emergency vehicles; smart buses will have GPS tracking and real-time updates via a mobile app, per Transportation Department director David Chung.
Smart surveillance cameras with facial recognition are scheduled for mid-2024; Community Police Chief Anita Rodriguez said they will follow strict privacy guidelines.
An interactive website and mobile app for resident feedback and city information are slated for release by the end of February 2024.
Air quality sensors are due by March 2024, and water quality sensors will be deployed in local waterways.

Challenges include integrating extensive hardware and software into existing urban infrastructure and addressing privacy and security concerns; the City Council is finalizing the strategic implementation plan.
